Either answer is fair. They tell me different things about you."

I told her it does not, and that she should take no comfort from that."

"You have it," Corse says pleasantly. "Rourke wrote that evening and apologised. I told him it is no hanging matter and he must not dock anybody." He points to the chair. "Do sit. It changes nothing. I would like to explain why."

The wardens have been taken out through the kitchen. Corse sits at the desk, writing with a cloth round two fingers. "I shall not do that again," he says. "Not for your sake, for theirs. The total is correct; I checked it. Then it says what is to be done. I will not tell you what that is. You would ask whether I mean to do it, and I have not decided."

"I tell you so you do not build an idea of your importance out of rumour. Rumour is flattering. Eleven hundred and sixty gold is a bad quarter. It is not a war."

the_instruction.text: "I do, within a figure," Corse says. "They give me a sum and a year. I spend it as well as I can, and they judge me on the return." He says it without pride or apology. "That is how I can answer you. There is no secret to it. There is a figure, and I am answerable for it. I will be next year, too."

the_mark_question.text: "The bob and the square," he says, finding a note in the desk and holding it up. "It is the house mark, used since my grandfather. It is no signal; it is like writing your name in a book."

the_plate.text: "That would be the Fenmoor lot," Corse says after a moment. I did not ask, and I should have." He pauses. "I am not surprised. Goods go where the price takes them."

somebody_did.text: "We sold to a man who sold to another man," Corse says. "That is different from arming them ourselves. I can give you the Greyhythe buyer's name. the_stone.text: "Then one of our surveyors has been down there," Corse says. "I would expect that. A man cannot sign for land he has not walked." He rolls his pen between his fingers. why_rivermark.text: "It is where the road runs," Corse says. "Everything from the head of the valley must pass through town or go forty miles round. That is Rivermark, as far as the accounts are concerned: the narrow part." He stops, then says, "I know that is a poor thing to say about eleven hundred people. But it is why the house is interested. I would be lying if I dressed it up."

nothing_at_all.text: "Nothing at all," Corse says. "That is what a retainer is for. You are not paid to do a particular thing. then_we_understand.text: "Then we understand each other," Corse says, writing it down. "I will tell you what happens next, since you will find out anyway. The house will want a name. They will ask me, and I will give the true answer: I do not know. They will not believe me. A man will come up from downriver who is not a factor and does not answer questions." He looks up. "That is not a threat. It is a schedule."

Not anger, perhaps regret at being understood too late. "You did the right thing. It did not work, and I want you to know I see that."

he_grants_it.text: "They know," Corse agrees. "That is something. In nineteen years, it is the only thing anyone has taken from me that I could not put back." He turns his pen on the desk. "Come back in the spring. There will be more to say, and I would rather say it to you than to whoever they send."

a_bad_quarter.text: "At a good deal more than that, it stops being mine," Corse says. "I am a man with a district and a figure I answer for. While the loss is a figure I can carry, it stays between you and me. I will still give you the chair and the ham. If it grows beyond that, it goes downriver in the quarterly return. Men who have never walked this valley compare it with eleven others and decide what to do about the valley losing money." He turns his glass. "They are not cruel. They have never seen the place. I have watched that happen twice, and it is worse."

he_has_not_decided.text:
"Whether to write back," Corse says. "That is all. There is no other decision available, and I would not want you to think there is." He looks towards the crane. "If I write back, I am a factor arguing with the house over four people who walked here. I have one such letter in me, and I have been saving it for eleven years. If I do not, ordinary people will do it in the ordinary way, and none of them will ever have met you.

"I am telling you because you have never lied to me in this room, and I find I mind about that. Do not mistake it for an alliance. I would like you to leave the valley."
